title: Annual component estimates gave 21% more supply variance than a zero-covariance reference in Superior and Michigan-Huron, 1950-2022
abstract: We tested whether evaporation offsets or amplifies variation in precipitation plus runoff within two Great Lakes. We used L2SWBM V3.0 monthly component medians for 1950-2022 and summed them by calendar year. Annual net basin supply variance was 20.95% above a zero-covariance reference for Superior and 21.04% above it for Michigan-Huron. Conditional 97.5% five-year block intervals were 4.54% to 38.97% and 7.98% to 34.82%. Input-evaporation correlations were -0.276 and -0.308. Thus, lower evaporation tended to occur with larger water inputs in this reconstruction. Trend removal and an October-September year kept this result. The recent Superior subset was less clear. These are arithmetic results for reconstructed component medians. They do not identify a physical feedback or include posterior model uncertainty. We provide exact source hashes, monthly inputs, annual evidence, saved resamples, all checks, code, and a figure.

display.caption: Annual input and evaporation anomalies, and the supply variance ratio Q. Q is the variance of P + R - E divided by the sum of the variances of P + R and E. Values above 1 show amplification relative to zero covariance. Bars show conditional 97.5% block intervals. Only the two primary annual intervals form the planned 95% family. Checks are sensitivity results.
